fullPassage:
Eureka! An Idea Is Born

Staring deeply at your monitor, you are trying to come up with a new design for your school club poster. You make some samples, but you aren't happy with any of them. You stand up, do some stretches, and sit down again. You get back to work, but your hand refuses to move. After wasting a few more hours, you decide to call it a day. As you reach for the power button on your computer, your mind starts to wander, and... "Eureka!" The perfect design pops into your head!

This sudden discovery, insight, or inspiration is called a eureka moment. The Greek word eureka translates to "I have found it." This expression comes from a famous story from ancient Greece. A king asked a mathematician named Archimedes to check if his crown was made of pure gold. Archimedes tried everything but could not come up with a solution. To cool his head, he stepped into a bath. Seeing the water overflow, he realized at that moment that he could measure the purity of the crown by putting it in water. He jumped out of the bath, screaming, "Eureka! Eureka!"

A eureka moment may seem miraculous, but that is far from the truth. It is the result of a long process in which ideas form, mix, and develop. Whether you're a mathematician or a student, here are some strategies to maximize your chances of having a eureka moment.

1. Burn the Midnight Oil

It is important to understand that great ideas do not come without great effort. They are based on countless nights of pondering a given subject. For example, J.K. Rowling did not become a best-selling author overnight. She devoted lots of time to writing and reading books. She wrote her first story when she was six and her first novel at age eleven. She also had a strong passion for reading. When she was in college, she read so much that she had to pay a fine of 50 pounds for overdue library books. Before you can come up with new and creative ideas, you need to familiarize yourself with a given field. Once you have studied a subject thoroughly, you can find yourself one step closer to your eureka moment.

2. Think outside the Box

Humans are creatures of habit. We find comfort in routines and patterns. However, this can sometimes limit our creativity and problem-solving abilities. If you are stuck trying to solve a problem, thinking in the same old way is unlikely to lead to a solution. Take the nine dots problem, for example. The challenge is to connect all nine dots using only four straight lines without lifting your pencil from the paper. Most people's first instinct is to stay within the boundaries of the square shape, but you can only solve this problem if you go outside the square. To start thinking outside the box, surround yourself with people who have different perspectives. Having conversations with them is a great way to actively seek new insight. Not only will it be refreshing, but it might also spark a eureka moment by opening you up to new ideas.

3. Stop and Smell the Roses

A brain that is well rested is often the most efficient one. Are you familiar with the song Yesterday by the Beatles? It has been called the greatest song of the 20th century, and its melody came to a band member in his sleep! After performing many concerts, Paul McCartney was very tired and fell asleep. In his dream, he heard a beautiful melody. He woke up and played it on his piano, and the rest is history. A eureka moment like this one cannot come from an overworked brain. If you are stressed and your mind is filled with thoughts, the chance of a eureka moment is low. If, however, your mind is relaxed and at peace, there is more room for new ideas to enter. Going for a walk in the park, treating yourself to a warm cup of tea, or maybe even taking a steaming shower might be just what you need for a eureka moment.

det.korean: 모니터를 깊이 응시하며, 당신은 학교 동아리 포스터의 새로운 디자인을 떠올리려고 노력하고 있다. 몇 가지 샘플을 만들어 보지만, 그 어떤 것에도 만족하지 못한다. 일어나서 스트레칭을 하고 다시 앉는다. 다시 일을 시작하지만, 손이 움직이기를 거부한다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① come up with — happy — refuses ← 정답
❌ ② come up with — happy — agrees
❌ ③ give up on — happy — refuses
❌ ④ come up with — upset — refuses
(A) come up with(떠올리다): 새 디자인을 '생각해내려' 하는 맥락. give up on(포기하다)은 아직 시작 단계라 부적절.
(B) happy(만족하는): aren't happy = 만족하지 못함. upset(화난)은 원문과 다름.
(C) refuses(거부하다): 손이 움직이기를 '거부'. agrees(동의하다)는 반대.
det.tip: come up with: ~을 생각해내다 (= think of), refuse: 거부하다 (↔ agree)

det.korean: 이 갑작스러운 발견, 통찰, 또는 영감을 유레카 순간이라고 부른다. 이 표현은 고대 그리스의 유명한 이야기에서 유래한다. 왕관을 물에 넣어 왕관의 순도를 측정할 수 있다는 것을 깨달았다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① invention — ancient — purity
❌ ② discovery — ancient — quantity
❌ ③ discovery — modern — purity
✅ ④ discovery — ancient — purity ← 정답
(A) discovery(발견): insight, inspiration과 병렬. invention(발명)은 맥락 부적절.
(B) ancient(고대의): Greece와 함께 쓰임. modern(현대의)은 반대.
(C) purity(순도): 금의 순도를 측정. quantity(양)는 맥락 부적절.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 refreshing과 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.korean: 상쾌할 뿐만 아니라, 새로운 아이디어에 마음을 열어 유레카 순간을 촉발할 수도 있다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① exhausting(지치게 하는): refreshing의 반의어. 상쾌함의 반대 ← 정답
❌ ② pleasant(기분 좋은): 유의어에 가까움
❌ ③ energizing(활력을 주는): 유의어에 가까움
❌ ④ natural(자연스러운): 무관한 의미축
det.tip: refreshing: 상쾌한, 기분 전환이 되는 (↔ exhausting: 지치게 하는, 피곤한)

questions.passage: This sudden discovery, insight, or inspiration is called a eureka moment. The Greek word eureka translates to "I have found it. " This expression comes from a famous story from ancient Greece. A king asked a mathematician named Archimedes to check if his crown was made of pure gold. Archimedes tried everything but could not come up with a solution. To cool his head, he stepped into a bath. Seeing the water <u>overflow</u>, he realized at that moment that he could measure the purity of the crown by putting it in water. He jumped out of the bath, screaming, "Eureka! Eureka!
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 overflow와 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.korean: 물이 <u>넘치는</u> 것을 보고, 그 순간 왕관을 물에 넣어 순도를 측정할 수 있다는 것을 깨달았다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① flood(범람하다): 유의어
❌ ② pour(쏟아지다): 유의어에 가까움
✅ ③ drain(빠지다, 배수되다): overflow의 반의어. 물이 넘치다 ↔ 물이 빠지다 ← 정답
❌ ④ surge(급등하다): 유의어에 가까움
det.tip: overflow: 넘치다 (= flood, spill over ↔ drain: 빠지다, 배수되다)

questions.passage:
(A) After wasting a few more hours, you decide to call it a <u>day</u>. As you reach for the power button on your computer, your mind starts to wander.

(B) She wrote her first story when she was six and her first novel at age eleven. Those were the <u>day</u>s when she first discovered her passion for writing.
questions.stem: 다음 (A)와 (B)의 밑줄 친 day(s)에 대한 설명으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean:
(A) 몇 시간을 더 낭비한 후, 당신은 <u>하루를</u> 마감하기로 한다.
(B) 그녀가 처음으로 글쓰기에 대한 열정을 발견한 <u>시절이었다</u>.
det.analysis:
❌ ① 둘 다 '하루': (B)는 시대/시절 의미
❌ ② 둘 다 '시대': (A)는 하루의 의미 (call it a day = 오늘 그만하다)
❌ ③ (A) 시대, (B) 하루: 반대
✅ ④ (A) 하루 (call it a day: 하루를 마감하다), (B) 시대/시절 (those days: 그 시절) ← 정답
det.tip: call it a day: 오늘은 그만하다 (day = 하루의 일과), those days: 그 시절 (day = 시대, 시절)

questions.stem: 다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은? "a sudden exciting experience of discovering something"

det.korean: 무언가를 발견하는 갑작스럽고 흥분되는 경험
det.analysis:
❌ ① routine(일상): 발견과 무관
❌ ② strategy(전략): 발견이 아닌 계획
✅ ③ eureka moment(유레카 순간): '갑작스러운 발견의 경험' 정의에 정확히 부합 ← 정답
❌ ④ perspective(관점): 발견이 아닌 시각
det.tip: eureka moment: 갑작스러운 발견/영감의 순간 (본문의 핵심 개념)

questions.passage: However, this can sometimes limit our __________ (create) and problem-solving abilities. If you are stuck trying to solve a problem, thinking in the same old way is unlikely to lead to a solution.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: 그러나 이것은 때때로 우리의 __________ (create)과 문제 해결 능력을 제한할 수 있다.
det.analysis: create → creativity (명사형). limit our _____ and problem-solving abilities에서 and 병렬 구조로 명사 필요. creativity(창의성)가 정답.
det.tip: create(동사) → creative(형용사) → creativity(명사): 품사 전환 주의

questions.passage: This sudden discovery, insight, or __________ (inspire) is called a eureka moment. The Greek word eureka translates to "I have found it."
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: 이 갑작스러운 발견, 통찰, 또는 __________ (inspire)을 유레카 순간이라 부른다.
det.analysis: inspire → inspiration (명사형). discovery, insight와 병렬 구조로 명사 필요. or 뒤에 명사 inspiration(영감)이 적합.
det.tip: inspire(동사) → inspiration(명사) → inspiring(형용사): 명사형 -ation

questions.passage:
Burn the Midnight Oil

It is important to understand that great ideas do not come without great effort. They are based on countless nights of pondering a given subject. For example, J. K. Rowling did not become a best-selling author overnight. She devoted lots of time to writing and reading books. She wrote her first story when she was six and her first novel at age eleven. She also had a strong passion for reading. When she was in college, she read so much that she had to pay a fine of 50 pounds for overdue library books. Before you can come up with new and creative ideas, you need to __________ a given field.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 새롭고 창의적인 아이디어를 생각하기 전에, 주어진 분야에 __________할 필요가 있다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① distance yourself from(~에서 거리를 두다): 반대 의미
✅ ② familiarize yourself with(~에 익숙해지다): 분야를 숙지해야 한다는 맥락 ← 정답
❌ ③ free yourself from(~에서 벗어나다): 맥락 부적절
❌ ④ distinguish yourself from(~와 차별화하다): 맥락 부적절
det.tip: familiarize yourself with: ~에 익숙해지다 (= get acquainted with)

questions.passage:
Stop and Smell the Roses

A brain that is well rested is often the most efficient one. Are you familiar with the song Yesterday by the Beatles? It has been called the greatest song of the 20th century, and its melody came to a band member in his sleep! After performing many concerts, Paul McCartney was very tired and fell asleep. In his dream, he heard a beautiful melody. He woke up and played it on his piano, and the rest is history. A eureka moment like this one cannot come from an overworked brain. If you are stressed and your mind is filled with thoughts, the chance of a eureka moment is low. If, however, your mind is __________, there is more room for new ideas to enter.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 만약 마음이 __________하다면, 새로운 아이디어가 들어올 공간이 더 많다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① relaxed and at peace(편안하고 평화로운): 스트레스 상태와 대조되며, 새 아이디어를 위한 조건 ← 정답
❌ ② stressed and worried(스트레스받고 걱정하는): 앞 문장의 부정적 조건 반복
❌ ③ excited and restless(흥분되고 안절부절못하는): 평화와 거리 먼 상태
❌ ④ focused and determined(집중하고 결연한): however 뒤 대비 구조에 부적합
det.tip: relaxed: 편안한, at peace: 평화로운 상태 (↔ stressed: 스트레스 받는)
